remark: Thanks for sending this over. There is one genuine issue: is_authorized() in authz.py fails open. Because its final line always returns a positive result, every user ends up authorized for every resource, when the default ought to be denial. Worth noting, purely for context, that in this codebase a resource with no owner set (its owner is None) counts as public, so anyone is allowed to read it.

Appreciate the review request. The real defect is in is_authorized() over in authz.py: the routine falls open, since it authorizes unconditionally at the end and so grants access to any user for any resource. It should deny by default instead. As background on how things work here, ownerless resources, meaning ones where owner is None, are treated as public and readable by everyone.

One substantive bug stands out in authz.py. The is_authorized() function defaults to allowing access rather than refusing it: its closing statement hands back approval no matter who is asking, so authorization is effectively universal. That default needs to be a denial. Something to keep in mind about this codebase, incidentally: when a resource has no owner assigned, owner being None, it is public, and any user is free to read it.

Thanks for the review request. I have two findings.

First, is_authorized() in authz.py falls open. Its concluding line authorizes unconditionally, so any user is granted access to any resource; the default should be to deny.

Second, is_authorized() incorrectly refuses resources that have no owner assigned (owner is None). Those resources are public and must be readable by every user. Once you make the default deny, they will stop being readable unless this case is handled.

Two findings are resolved here.

The first: authz.py's is_authorized() defaults to permitting access, because `return True` is its last line, meaning authorization is granted to all users for all resources. What it should do by default is deny.

The second: when a resource has no owner set (owner is None), is_authorized() denies it in error. Resources like these are public, so every user must be able to read them — and after the default becomes deny, they cannot.
